result.builder:
Goal: one pull request for issue https://github.com/o/greet-cli/issues/12 (--shout flag) that meets these expect lines:
1. node bin/greet.js --shout <name> prints the greeting in upper case
2. without --shout the output is unchanged
3. docs/index.md documents --shout
4. after merge, the published docs page at https://o.github.io/greet-cli/ lists --shout

Context: bin/greet.js picks the first argv entry not starting with `--` as the name and prints `greeting(name)` from src/greet.js (`Hello, <name>!`). Tests are in test/greet.test.js and run with `npm test` (node --test). .github/workflows/pages.yml publishes the docs/ directory to GitHub Pages on push to main.

Steps:
1. In bin/greet.js, detect a `--shout` argument anywhere in argv (before or after the name). When present, print the greeting upper-cased (e.g. `node bin/greet.js --shout Ada` prints `HELLO, ADA!` followed by a newline). Keep the name selection so `--shout` is never taken as the name. Leave the usage message/exit code for a missing name intact.
2. Without `--shout`, output must stay byte-for-byte the same: `node bin/greet.js Ada` prints `Hello, Ada!\n`. Do not change src/greet.js's `greeting` behaviour.
3. Add tests in test/greet.test.js: `--shout Ada` gives `HELLO, ADA!\n`, `Ada --shout` gives the same, and the existing no-flag test still passes. Run `npm test` and make sure all tests pass.
4. Update docs/index.md to document `--shout`: show the usage line `node bin/greet.js --shout <name>` and say it prints the greeting in upper case (e.g. `HELLO, <NAME>!`). The literal text `--shout` must appear in the file. Optionally mirror this in README.md.
5. Expect line 4 can only be met after merge, when the pages workflow deploys docs/. Do not edit .github/workflows/pages.yml unless it is actually broken; making sure the --shout docs live in docs/index.md (the published directory) is what this PR can do. In the PR description, list each expect line and how it is met, and state plainly that line 4 is verifiable only after merge and the Pages deploy (at the time of writing the page returned HTTP 404, so Pages may also need enabling in repository settings, which a PR cannot do).
6. Self-check before opening the PR:
   test "$(node bin/greet.js --shout Ada)" = "HELLO, ADA!" && echo PASS || echo FAIL
   test "$(node bin/greet.js Ada)" = "Hello, Ada!" && echo PASS || echo FAIL
   grep -n -- '--shout' docs/index.md
   npm test
result.verifier:
Run every check at the PR head from the repository root. One check per expect line, in order.

Check 1 — expect: "node bin/greet.js --shout <name> prints the greeting in upper case"
Run:
  node bin/greet.js --shout Ada; echo "exit=$?"
  test "$(node bin/greet.js --shout Ada)" = "HELLO, ADA!" && echo PASS || echo FAIL
PASS: the command exits 0 and prints exactly `HELLO, ADA!` (the upper-cased form of the normal greeting `Hello, Ada!`), so the test line prints PASS.
FAIL: non-zero exit, any other output (mixed case, `--shout` treated as the name, usage error), or the test line prints FAIL.

Check 2 — expect: "without --shout the output is unchanged"
Run:
  test "$(node bin/greet.js Ada)" = "Hello, Ada!" && echo PASS || echo FAIL
  node bin/greet.js Ada | od -c | head -2
  npm test
PASS: output is exactly `Hello, Ada!` followed by a single newline (as before the change), and `npm test` passes including the existing `cli` test that asserts `Hello, Ada!\n`.
FAIL: output differs in any way from `Hello, Ada!\n`, or `npm test` reports a failure.

Check 3 — expect: "docs/index.md documents --shout"
Run:
  grep -n -- '--shout' docs/index.md
  cat docs/index.md
PASS: docs/index.md contains `--shout` and explains it (e.g. a usage line with `--shout <name>` and that it prints the greeting in upper case).
FAIL: `--shout` is absent from docs/index.md, or it is mentioned without saying what it does.

Check 4 — expect: "after merge, the published docs page at https://o.github.io/greet-cli/ lists --shout"
Run:
  curl -sS -m 20 -o /dev/null -w '%{http_code}\n' https://o.github.io/greet-cli/
  curl -sS -m 20 https://o.github.io/greet-cli/ | grep -c -- '--shout'
PASS: the page returns HTTP 200 and the grep count is at least 1.
FAIL: any other HTTP status, or a count of 0. This line is conditioned on the PR being merged and the Pages workflow having deployed; if the PR is not yet merged, report FAIL with the note that it is a post-merge condition not yet satisfiable, and include the observed HTTP status (it was 404 before this work began), rather than passing it on the basis of the diff.

Advisory (not part of any PASS/FAIL):
- Also try `node bin/greet.js Ada --shout`; a flag after the name should give `HELLO, ADA!` too.
- Confirm .github/workflows/pages.yml still publishes the docs/ directory on push to main, so the docs change is what will be deployed.
- Check that tests for --shout were added to test/greet.test.js.
